title: Numerical Linear Algebra, Explained: Twenty Problem Resolutions
abstract: Lean formalizations accompanying twenty numerical linear algebra problem resolutions. They give uniform matrix-product growth and local 1/d-Hölder continuity of the joint spectral radius; two real generators with any prescribed nonnegative polynomial growth exponent; and sharp losses 2^r and 4^r for randomly pivoted Cholesky and LU. They show that concave matrix functions can destroy spectral approximation guarantees and amplify nuclear-norm excess without bound, and give sharp Frobenius transfer bounds with and without semidefinite order. Further results are the random-row adversarial deletion limit and sharp universal deletion constant, a pointwise strict tensor-train bound with unchanged worst-case supremum, and curves with rank savings delayed through any prescribed finite range of tensor powers. Counterexamples concern derivative roots of nonnegative characteristic polynomials, a q-permanent subset inequality, a geometric-mean norm inequality, and weighted log-majorisation. The development also proves the rectangular Rowland-Wu Sinkhorn identity, disconnected quotients of minimal positive semidefinite factors, stable nonsynchronised equilibria on random cubic graphs with high probability, and NP-hardness of exact determinant ranges and solution hulls for regular tridiagonal interval matrices. This repository prepares the proofs for Palomar through a single repository-root Challenge/Solution interface selecting all twenty problem resolutions. Seventeen component environments have recorded Lean 4.35.0 compilation and selected-axiom checks; the combined environment has separate current evidence. Official Palomar and independent NanoDa verification remain pending submission.
